Home.heroBody: Excellence AI is an enterprise MCP server: the secure, standard connection between AI tools and company systems. Your team keeps its familiar tools; you control access, approvals, and the audit trail.
Home.featureMcpBody: No new chatbot to roll out. Your team keeps working in the AI tools they know, while Excellence AI connects them securely to company systems.
Home.featureAccessBody: You decide who can access each company system. Sensitive actions only run after a human approves them.
Home.featureAuditBody: Every AI action is logged: who asked for it, which data was accessed, and what happened. Everything can be reviewed later.
Home.featureAdminBody: Company administrators manage AI agents, system connections, roles, and autonomy. Only approved capabilities are available.
Home.featureModelsBody: Claude, Hermes, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok — your team uses what works. Company governance always stays in Excellence AI.

scheduledTasks.body: Recurring work that an AI coworker does on your own computer or in the cloud — for example every weekday morning. The platform only records and coordinates it; your AI client runs it.
scheduledTasks.help: Here you set what the coworker should do and when. The AI client on your computer (e.g. Claude) offers to install it the next time you open it; from then on its own scheduler starts it. Even if it is installed in two places, it runs only once per scheduled time.

GetStarted.hermesDesc: With your own model key, for a quick try
GetStarted.hermesIntro: In Hermes Desktop every AI coworker gets its own Bot. The Bot is only a connector: role, skills and memory come from the platform every session. You see and approve the work here, and no passwords are stored on your machine. No plugin needed: stock Hermes is enough.
GetStarted.hermesStep1Body: Download it from the official site (version 0.21.5 or later) and start it.
GetStarted.hermesStep2Body: On first start Hermes walks you through choosing an AI model and entering its API key. You can change this later in Settings → Model.
GetStarted.hermesStep2Hint: Bots receive only this provider's key. Your other keys stay in the default profile.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Body: Click the button below. Hermes Desktop opens and asks you to confirm the server — check that the name is excellence. Then click Authorize; your browser opens. Sign in with the same account you use here.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Manual: If the button does nothing: Capabilities → MCP → Import, paste your organization MCP URL from above, name the server excellence, choose OAuth, save, then Authorize.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Hint: Keep the server name excellence — Bots reach the platform under this name. In the MCP tab you should see tools listed when the connection works.
GetStarted.hermesAdvancedTerminalBody: If you already use the terminal, you can run this command instead:
GetStarted.hermesStep4Body: In the Hermes chat (default profile), type:
GetStarted.hermesStep4Hint: Hermes creates a thin connector for each AI coworker you can access (name, MCP, agent-id). Role, skills and memory come from the platform, not from disk. For each Bot a browser opens once for approval: sign in and accept.
GetStarted.hermesStep5Body: Open Bot Mode. Each coworker shows up as its own Bot, and you can start working in its chat right away.
GetStarted.hermesUpdateBody: Role and skills load live from the platform — you do not need to download the coworker again. If the connector (MCP URL or agent-id) changes, type the same sentence again in the default profile. Your Bots' chats, avatars and settings are kept.
GetStarted.hermesApprovalHint: Anything a Bot would change (for example sending an email) waits here, on the platform, for your approval.
GetStarted.hermesManagedLimits: In this version, local integration for company sandbox/cloud browser and trusted project roots, website and skill lists need additional implementation; Guard blocks when these are missing. Use company memory tools instead of native local memory. Guard heartbeat checks presence, not hardware attestation. Verify each Hermes version used.
GetStarted.hermesPersonalNote: In this mode you reach the model with your own key, so the company does not see your conversations, only your use of company tools. On a company computer, use Hermes Desktop Enterprise.
GetStarted.hermesEntDesc: Company model key and full company controls
GetStarted.hermesEntIntro: The same Bots, but the platform also provides the model. No model key is stored on your computer, and the company controls and logs AI traffic under its own rules. You do not need to pick a model.
GetStarted.hermesEntAdminTitle: What the admin and IT do
GetStarted.hermesEntAdminNote: Your company admin and IT prepare this: they set the company model key and install the company Hermes settings on your computer. If that has not happened yet, ask them before you start.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyBody: Bots use the company model key stored on the platform (OpenRouter or Gemini); no key goes onto employee computers. Add it under Settings → Company model keys.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyOk: The company model key is set.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyMissing: No company model key yet. Until there is one, Bots get no model responses.
GetStarted.hermesEntPolicyBody: Administration → Hermes company controls: select a company default and employee exceptions. Set a ceiling in Tools on the AI coworker page.
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallBody: Pick whose computer gets the company settings, and whether that computer is Mac / Linux or Windows. Download the installer, copy it to that computer, and run the command. First grant access to at least one active AI coworker — otherwise the computer blocks all local operations.
GetStarted.hermesEntDownloadFailed: Could not download the installer. Try again.
GetStarted.hermesEntNoMembers: There is no active employee to issue an installer for.
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallRun: Mac / Linux: copy the downloaded file to the employee computer, open Terminal in that folder, and run:
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallRunWindows: Windows: copy the downloaded file to the employee computer, open PowerShell as Administrator in that folder, and run:
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallHint: The installer applies the company settings and the Bot connectors. Then restart Hermes. The file is small; it is not the Hermes app.
GetStarted.hermesEntSecurityBody: IT should revoke model keys previously stored on the laptop. Company keys stay on the server. Use managed computers without employee admin rights, central deployment and outbound network rules; machine administrators can bypass local controls. After a new Bot profile or a wider permission, run the installer again.
GetStarted.hermesEntVerifyBody: After the employee has connected the platform: hermes config must show the managed settings and the excellence provider, and Bot Mode must show the installed Bots. Send a test message, check model and tool audit, and test a blocked operation and access revocation. Clients without Guard do not receive company model responses.
GetStarted.hermesEntStep1Body: If IT has not installed it yet, download it from the official site (version 0.21.5 or later). Restart it after the company settings are installed.
GetStarted.hermesEntNoModel: You do not need to enter a model or API key. If Hermes still asks for a key, the company settings are not on your computer yet: ask IT.
GetStarted.hermesEntBotsBody: The company installer already laid down the Bot connectors. Do not create Bots from chat on this computer — the chat cannot write Bot profiles. Open Bot Mode.
GetStarted.hermesEntBotsHint: For each Bot the browser opens once for platform sign-in: sign in and accept.
GetStarted.hermesEntTroubleshootTitle: If a Bot does not respond
GetStarted.hermesEntTroubleshootBody: Click Details on the error message. If it says `key_cmd for provider 'excellence' exited 1`, the Bot's sign-in to the platform has expired. Ask IT to run the latest company installer again, then close and reopen Hermes. If the error remains, IT can sign the Bot in again on your computer with the command below. Replace `<bot-profile>` with the Bot's folder name (for example, `exc-alfred`). The browser then opens: sign in and accept.
GetStarted.hermesEntUpdateBody: Role, skills and memory come live from the platform; there is no local copy. When a new AI coworker is added or access changes, run the installer again.

tips.access: Only switch on what they really need. “Read” is enough to start — you can allow writing later.
tips.knowledge: The more precise the documents, the more precise the answers. Policies, price lists and FAQs work best.
tips.autonomy: Start as Trainee: they ask before every write. Once you trust them, give more independence.
tips.team: To start, it is enough if only you can see them. Once it works, share with the team in one click.
tips.advanced: Feel free to skip this step — the defaults suit most teammates.
tips.launch: After putting them to work, try the suggested questions. If something is off, come back and change it any time.

Attach one here without writing code: enter the address, review and approve its tools, then assign it to a teammate under Connections. Credentials stay on the platform; every call is logged.

filter.title: Privacy filter
filter.intro: Before a request reaches the AI model, the company server can check it for personal or confidential data (card numbers, social security numbers, email addresses). The filter protects data but makes work harder: the model sees placeholders instead of real values and some requests are not sent. Turn it on only where people really handle sensitive data (e.g. finance, HR, customer service).

off.title: Off
off.help: Requests are not checked. Nothing slows down work, but there are no privacy signals either.

observe.title: Observe only
observe.help: Every request goes out unchanged. If sensitive data is found, the log records which kind and how many (never the data itself).

enforce.title: On
enforce.help: Per data type: replaces it with a placeholder, allows company models only, or does not send the request. Use only when justified.

filter.enforceWarning: When the filter is on, the model sees placeholders (e.g. [[PHONE_1]]) which we turn back into the real values in the answer. If a data type is set to “Block the request”, the user cannot continue that conversation until they remove the data or start a new conversation.
filter.categoriesTitle: What should happen with each data type?
filter.categoriesHelp: Applies to every message: the user's text, attached file content and tool results.
filter.categoriesInactive: These settings only take effect when the filter is on. In “Observe only” mode the log and the test show what would happen.
filter.limits: The filter looks for known patterns. A person's name is only recognised when it appears together with an email address (e.g. “John Smith '<'john@company.com'>'”), and after that anywhere in the conversation. Company names are not recognised on this path yet.

levelHelp.block: If the request contains this data, it is not sent and the user gets a clear message about what to remove.
levelHelp.local_only: Only the company's self-hosted AI model may receive it. If none is configured, the request is not sent.
levelHelp.tokenize: The model sees a placeholder; the real value is restored in the answer and in data passed to tools.
levelHelp.warn: The request goes out unchanged; the log records that such data was sent.
levelHelp.off: This data type is not watched. (Card numbers and IBANs going out are still logged.)
